outcome: Gottschalk's surjunctivity conjecture (is every group surjunctive?) remains open. The only claimed full proof (Cannizzo, arXiv:1912.00541, 'All groups are surjunctive') predates the frozen revision and was withdrawn by its author two days after posting in December 2019 due to a fatal gap in Lemma 5.3/Theorem 5.4; it was never resurrected. Post-window papers (2024-2026) extend surjunctivity-type results to sofic groups, non-uniform cellular automata, and invariant random subgroups, but none settles a new case of, or narrows, the general conjecture for all groups.
summary: The core question — is every group surjunctive (Gottschalk's surjunctivity conjecture) — remains open as of September 2026. The one attempt at a full resolution, Jan Cannizzo's December 2019 preprint claiming all finitely generated groups are surjunctive (arXiv:1912.00541), predates the frozen revision by over four years and, more importantly, was withdrawn by the author himself two days after the initial submission (v2, 2019-12-04), who stated the last sentence of Lemma 5.3 is unjustified and 'likely counts as a fatal flaw that invalidates the main theorem.' This is a pre-window, withdrawn claim, not a post-window event, so it does not move the status; I record it under 'event' only as the most recent substantive attempt on the conjecture, with predates_frozen_revision=true, and status is coded open/no_change_found rather than open_stale or progress/incident, since the withdrawal itself is also pre-window (no post-2024-01-26 development attaches to it). I searched for any 2024-2026 developments and found three papers, all variants under the §3.1 scope rule rather than cases or narrowings of the core conjecture: (1) arXiv:2403.05998 ('Generalized Gottschalk's conjecture for sofic groups and applications', March 2024) extends known surjunctivity-type theorems (Gromov-Weiss, Capobianco-Kari-Taati) to local perturbations of cellular automata and twisted group rings over sofic group universes — it assumes sofic groups are surjunctive (already known via Gromov-Weiss, itself pre-2024) and generalizes the automata/ring-theoretic apparatus around that fact, rather than settling surjunctivity for any group not already known to be surjunctive. (2) arXiv:2503.23435 ('On Gottschalk's Surjunctivity Conjecture for Non-uniform Cellular Automata', March 2025) proves a reversibility/invertibility result for non-uniform cellular automata over group universes that are already assumed surjunctive — a different (derived) question, not a case of 'is G surjunctive.' (3) arXiv:2511.06586 ('Surjunctivity does not characterize cosoficity of invariant random subgroups', November 2025) answers a related but distinct question in the negative — whether surjunctivity of an invariant random subgroup implies cosoficity — which is about IRSs, not about whether groups themselves are surjunctive. None of these three papers reduces the space of groups for which surjunctivity is unknown, and none is a restriction of the stated question in the sense of §3.1 (a case obtained by restricting the domain of the same question); they are variants that change the question (different objects: NUCA reversibility, IRS cosoficity) or extensions of the toolkit around an already-known class (sofic groups). The Wikipedia article on surjunctive groups, checked live, still states 'It is unknown whether every group is surjunctive' with no post-2014 developments mentioned. No AI involvement was found in any of the three post-window papers or in the withdrawn 2019 preprint; all rely on classical techniques in symbolic dynamics, descriptive set theory, and group theory, with no mention of machine learning, automated theorem proving, or AI assistance in any abstract, methodology, or acknowledgement section I could access.
competing_reading: One could argue the November 2025 IRS/cosoficity paper (arXiv:2511.06586) is close enough to the surjunctivity apparatus that it constitutes 'progress' in the broader research program around surjunctivity, since it resolves a natural companion question (does surjunctivity of an IRS imply cosoficity) in the negative. But the stated bullet is specifically 'is every group surjunctive', a question about groups, not about invariant random subgroups; the IRS question is a different mathematical object with its own conjecture (cosoficity vs. surjunctivity for IRSs), so under the change-vs-restrict test it is a related problem, not a case, and does not change what a careful reader would write in this bullet's entry.
what_would_settle_it: A preprint or announcement that either exhibits a non-surjunctive group (a counterexample, refuting the conjecture) or proves surjunctivity for a new class of groups not already covered by Gromov-Weiss sofic-group surjunctivity or other known classes (partial progress), or a corrected/re-submitted version of the Cannizzo argument (or an independent proof) that survives expert scrutiny (resolution).
